name: Brightstar Lottery PLC
reason: Lottery concessions (Italian Lotto, US state contracts) are durable but adjusted EPS fell from USD 2.33 (2016) to 0.91 (2025) with a 65% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap, 2.5x net debt/EBITDA and concession re-tender risk after the gaming divestiture, so 5-10y earnings cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: Cementos Molins SA
reason: Family-controlled cement producer whose EPS of EUR 2.92 (2025) is at its 10y high after a construction/pricing upswing, consensus FY2-FY3 growth is only ~2.7%/yr and cement is a cyclical commodity with no specialness.

name: Mediobanca Banca di Credito Finanziario SpA
reason: Adjusted EPS grew from EUR 0.68 to 1.72 (FY2016-26) but 10y avg ROE is only 8.5%, earnings mix CIB/capital-markets and consumer credit, and the 2025 takeover by Monte dei Paschi (now parent, low free float) makes strategy and minority treatment unforecastable.

name: MONETA Money Bank AS
reason: Czech retail/consumer-credit bank with good 15.9% avg ROE but EPS fell 42% in 2020, 2025 EPS of CZK 12.71 is a peak-rate 10y high and consensus FY2-FY3 growth is only 6.7%/5.6% with LTG 2.8%, failing the US bank standard of a >=7% non-NIM route.

name: SNAM SpA
reason: Regulated Italian gas network (CDP ~30% holder) with EPS EUR 0.28 to 0.41 over 2015-25 (~4%/yr), 6.3x net debt/EBITDA and consensus LTG 4.4% - forecastable but growth set by ARERA allowed returns and well below 7%.

name: Verbio SE
reason: Biofuel producer whose earnings are set by commodity spreads and regulatory quotas: EPS swung from EUR 4.89 (2022) to -2.17 (FY2025) and is at 0.19x its 10y max.

name: Sagax AB
reason: High-quality property compounder (FFO/share SEK 2.41 to 11.45 over 2015-25) but growth came from acquisitions funded by 8.8x net debt/EBITDA and 3.9%/yr share issuance, FFO stalled in 2025 (+0.4%) and consensus is ~3%/yr - a rate-cycle levered growth model.

name: Valiant Holding AG
reason: Swiss domestic retail bank with 10y avg ROE of only 5.5%, EPS CAGR 4.8% and consensus FY2-FY3 growth ~6% - safe but ordinary, failing the best-in-class bank test.

name: Romande Energie Holding SA
reason: Canton-controlled Swiss electricity utility with volatile EPS (CHF 8.28 in 2023 to 0.95 in 2024), 10y avg ROE 4.2% and near-zero FCF conversion (0.01) - no growth route or specialness.

name: NP3 Fastigheter AB
reason: Northern-Sweden secondary-location industrial/commercial landlord with 8.4x net debt/EBITDA, acquisitions at 1.3x FCF and consensus FY2-FY3 FFO growth of -0.5%/+3.7% - leverage-driven growth with no moat.

name: Aalberts NV
reason: Acquisitive industrial (acq/FCF 0.71) with adjusted EPS EUR 3.36 (2022) down to 2.54 (2025), 10y EPS CAGR 4.5%, ROIC ~9.7% and a 42% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap - cyclical and ordinary.

name: Vontobel Holding AG
reason: Swiss wealth/asset manager whose earnings track market levels and structured-product activity (EPS -38% in 2022, CHF 6.50 in 2021 to 4.90 in 2025) with consensus LTG of 1% - capital-markets earner per the US standard.

name: Alimak Group AB
reason: Vertical-access equipment maker whose growth came from acquisitions (acq/FCF 1.39, Tractel deal) and 5.4%/yr share issuance, ROIC averages 6.5% and EBIT margin of 14.6% is at the 91st pctile of its history in a construction-cyclical end market.

name: Severn Trent Plc
reason: Regulated UK water utility with negative FCF (-8.4% yield), 7.0x net debt/EBITDA, 2.4%/yr share issuance, ROIC 2.7% and returns set by Ofwat/political intervention - forecastable rate base but not a Buffett business.

name: OMV Petrom SA
reason: Integrated oil & gas producer (Romanian state ~21%, OMV 51%) whose EPS is set by commodity prices and windfall taxes (RON 0.16 in 2022 to 0.08 in 2025, 0.52x 10y max).

name: Volex Plc
reason: Contract cable/power-cord maker whose EPS growth (USD 0.01 to 0.43) was driven by acquisitions (acq/FCF 1.28) and 7.6%/yr share issuance, with EBIT margin at a 100th-pctile 8.8% and a 37% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap - commodity-like manufacturing without a moat.

name: QinetiQ Group plc
reason: Decent defence test & evaluation franchise (ROIC ~12%, net debt 0.5x, consensus ~10%) but earnings depend on UK MoD long-term contracts and the US unit was written down in FY2024 (EPS -12%), the same government-contract concentration that kept BAH/LDOS TOO HARD.

name: United Utilities Group Plc
reason: Regulated UK water utility with negative FCF (-7.5% yield), 6.2x net debt/EBITDA, ROIC 2.6%, EPS of GBP 1.07 at a 100th-pctile margin after the PR24 reset and consensus growth of ~3-4%/yr.

name: Babcock International Group Plc
reason: Government defence/nuclear services contractor with adjusted EPS of GBP 0.39 (2025) at 0.46x its 2018 high, 10y avg ROIC 1.9% and a history of contract write-downs - a turnaround, not a durable compounder.

name: Akzo Nobel NV
reason: Paints/coatings maker with flat 10y EPS (EUR 3.61 in 2015 to 3.63 in 2025, CAGR 0.1%), revenue CAGR -3.7%, 4.0x net debt/EBITDA and EBIT margin at a 9th-pctile 3.5% amid restructuring and the pending Axalta merger - no forecastable growth route.
